title: LOBSTER promotion ledger

mirroredFrom.rule: THIS IS A VERBATIM COPY. Edit the ledger on claude/cluster-lookahead and re-copy the whole tools/learnloop/ directory here; never the other way round. A divergence is resolved by re-copying, not by merging — one of the two is the record and the other is a convenience.

readMe: ONE ARTIFACT, TWO CONSUMERS. The cloud coordinator reads this to know what has
been settled; the local sim session reads it to know what to run next.
`bin/make-promotion-batch.js` turns it into the next batch's spec files, so
'what should the PC run next?' is a command and not a judgement call.
THE ONE RULE THIS LEDGER EXISTS TO ENFORCE: a deterministic probe is NECESSARY
AND NEVER SUFFICIENT. CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED passed its deterministic ship gate
outright (fatal stagings 41 -> 0) and then lost snake6 1.00 -> 0.15 live, through
exhaustion — a travel-economy channel the probe does not measure. Only a live
paired sweep, with a concurrent verified null and a VERIFIED ENGAGED treatment
arm, may write a live status.

statusLadder: dark -> probe-passed  : a deterministic probe cleared its gate. Goes no further.
probe-passed -> live-* : only a live paired sweep with a verified concurrent null.
supported -> promoted  : the default flip was actually made; `promotedBy` names the commit.
frozen                 : re-opened by a MECHANISM CLAIM only, never by a p-value.
explorationSliceRule: A promoted or supported flag keeps ~10% of its cells running the OPPOSITE branch,
forever. Today's policy selects tomorrow's corpus, so a cell that turned a flag on
will otherwise never generate the data by which it could be turned back off.
powerArithmetic: A block is one seed through every cyclic seat rotation (3 games on a 3-team board).
Placement: 80% power at MDE 0.25 needs ~58 blocks on the pooled stratum, 8 on the
tightest (mix23 alone); MDE 0.10 needs 362-1,447. That is 360-1,000+ games per cell
PER ARM. Mechanism metrics move at n~8 blocks and are 5-25x outside the null band.
So: refit on mechanism, describe placement, and refuse a placement verdict from a
cell whose blocksHad < blocksNeeded. (A3 memo section 4.1.)
retiredCounters: plansEvaluated and boundsInversions are RETIRED as verdict-bearing metrics on any
live arm: at any budget they are dominated by how much CPU the process got. They
carry a verdict ONLY under a fixed-tick StepClock A/A, where the arms consume
identical work by construction. They are still reported, because they diagnose a
armEngagementRule: A live measurement must carry armEngagementVerified. `false` records the row and
moves nothing: a null from an arm that never ran is a different finding from a null
from an arm that ran and did not help. P5 is the standing exhibit — CENTAUR_WASM is
refused per partition, silently, whenever an input is not resident in linear memory.
CL7's mechanism report (TeamTurnResult.mechanism) is what makes the answer readable.

measurements.value: fatal stagings 41 -> 0; teammate kills 25 -> 4; rung-0 floor better on 18/26, mean +43.07; two -Infinity emissions rescued; emissions 57 -> 32

measurements.note: The effect is an order of magnitude outside the cell's own null band, so power is not the question here.

measurements.value: snake exhaustion deaths x1.9 (39 -> 75 over 48 games)
measurements.note: THE MECHANISM. The pairwise seed appears to disrupt snake parallel-motion and food economics — travel economy, not staging safety. The deterministic gate measures positions; this is the shape of a whole game.

measurements.note: So the cost is the seed's, not the pair's. UNIT_FATALITY alone carried no placement cost.

openInstrumentItems.what: A3 section 4.2 item 5 asks every emission to carry {policy, detectors:{sliderPresent, ownTrail, promotionImminent}, profile}. No production producer emits it, so the DETECTOR flip rate — the quantity A3's hysteresis signal is actually about — cannot be computed from a committed batch.
openInstrumentItems.workaround: bin/ingest.js emits a PAIRED OUTCOME flip rate and labels it as a proxy.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: not CL7. It needs a detector-state field on the emission path, which is a decision-path change and outside a telemetry-only stage.

openInstrumentItems.what: CENTAUR_EDGE_EV's primary mechanism metric is uncontested-meals-staged by contest class. The harness records deaths and health, not staged eats split that way.
openInstrumentItems.workaround: mine the replay's per-turn food events; the data is in the committed replays.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: a miner in tools/learnloop, or a harness counter. Neither is a decision-path change.

openInstrumentItems.what: The arch/s2 cohort governor publishes no counter the mechanism report can fold, so P6's null is engagement-unverified by construction.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: arch/s2 adding its own report and CL7's mechanismReportOf folding it, after that branch merges.

openInstrumentItems.what: ports.env reaches the wire policy, the worker count and the WASM default. It does NOT reach the five search-side flags or the two candidate knobs, which read process.env directly. An env-injecting caller therefore runs a different arm from the one it thinks it set.
openInstrumentItems.impact: None on the sim harness, which sets process-level environment per bundle. It is a trap for any in-process paired arm.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: threading ports.env into flaggedKnobs() and the five *Enabled() helpers — which changes which arm an env-injecting caller runs, so it is a behaviour change and not a CL7 item.

standingExperiments.title: The budget ladder
standingExperiments.approvedBy: owner — pre-approved, conditional on budget-probe v2 confirming
standingExperiments.trigger: CONFIRMED. budget-probe v2: a true 1000 ms run reproduces the 2000 ms decision 91.7% of the time (flip 8.3 +/- 7.0 against an A/A floor of 1.7 +/- 3.2). The engine is deadline-aware; the second second changes about 7% of decisions net. The condition on the pre-approval is met.
standingExperiments.question: Where on the budget curve does the substrate stop being speed and start being strength? P1 found the perf substrate was speed-not-strength at 2000 ms; the bimodal revision result (65% of decisions settle by 250 ms, 34.8% revise in a wave at 1000-1500 ms, nothing between) says 1000 ms would amputate the second pass entirely. Three points draw the line.
standingExperiments.designNote: ONE trail-instrumented cell in the ladder. The 35% revision wave was measured PRE-CL3, and cluster enumeration front-loads coordination, so the wave's own shape may have moved — which would make the ladder's middle rung mean something different from what it meant last month. Mechanism-first at 8 blocks: placement is descriptive here, not claimable.
standingExperiments.caveat: changed != improved. The 35.0% figure counts decisions whose staged move-set CHANGED after the 1000 ms mark; nothing in it says the later set is better. Probe v1 was RETRACTED (a shared engine carried per-game ledger state); v2 is the valid one.
